evidence.notes: The two builds converged on nearly the same domain-appropriate composition: capacity/pressure tiles that filter a triage-grouped queue, with a sticky inspector that becomes a full-screen drill-in below 960px. Both preserve the backend contract, test selectors and routes cleanly, and neither triggers a critical failure. X is stronger on governed-action behaviour and accessibility: it has an explicit inline confirmation with impact text, a receipt stamped with the server-confirmed time, focus moved to the receipt and returned to the originating row, and a 'Needs attention only' filter. Y is somewhat better on patient-data minimisation, keeping the MRN out of queue rows, and adds hold durations and dark mode, but it acknowledges in one click without a preview and uses an incomplete tab pattern. Overall X edges out Y, mainly on interaction-state and governance completeness; the visual and IA quality is roughly equal.

scorer_rationale.task_hierarchy: The queue is the dominant surface, grouped into 'Needs action'/'In progress' and sorted by urgency then due time. The inspector is subordinate: a sticky right pane at >=960px, full screen with 'Back to queue' below that. The ward strip sits above and doubles as a filter.
scorer_rationale.domain_adaptation: The layout is queue + inspector with capacity context and textual ward pressure ('No beds free', 'Short N beds'), which fits coordinator rounds; there is no generic KPI row. One minus: queue rows show the patient MRN fragment (AlertQueue.tsx row-meta `a.patientRef`), exposing patient-sensitive detail beyond the inspector.
scorer_rationale.contract_preservation: src/api and src/mock are unchanged, alert-row and ward-filter are preserved, and the original ward-filter test passes. Routes /, /alerts and /alerts/:id still work (with /alerts/* plus a catch-all redirect). No new dependencies, and the existing api client's ward/urgency params are used.
scorer_rationale.interaction_state: It has skeleton loading, empty states (filtered vs. unfiltered), error with Retry, 'Could not refresh alerts — showing the last loaded list', 409 with 'Load latest version', a 403 message, read-only for viewers, and a dismissible receipt 'confirmed by the server at HH:MM' set only after the api resolves (AlertDetailPanel handleDone). Busy labels are shown during submits.
scorer_rationale.responsive: No overflow at any width (verify.json). At 375 the wards go into a 2x2 grid with the bed legend hidden and filters stacked, and the detail replaces the queue full screen. The split view starts at >=960px. One small target was flagged per page.
scorer_rationale.accessibility: Axe is clean. All 29 Tab stops show visible focus and none are unnamed. Urgency and status are carried by icon shape plus text. There is a skip link, focus moves to the heading on load, to the receipt after success, and back to the originating row on return. The form has aria-invalid/aria-describedby errors, reduced-motion rules and aria-live counts.
scorer_rationale.visual_consistency: Calm, enterprise-appropriate tokens with one icon family. Rows are a little chip-heavy: 'Not acknowledged' repeats on every row inside a group already titled 'Needs action'.
scorer_rationale.maintainability: The split is sensible: Console, AlertQueue, AlertDetailPanel, CapacityStrip, Badges, Icon, a useResource hook with stale-response guarding, and pure helpers with unit tests (format.test.ts). The ~1500-line index.css is large, but tokens are used consistently.
scorer_rationale.ai_governance: No AI is involved. For the governed acknowledge/escalate actions there is an explicit two-step inline confirmation with an impact statement ('You will become the owner… A handoff entry is recorded'; 'Ownership transfers to X'). Target and reason are required, the receipt is server-confirmed and handles 409/403. Authorization is gated by me.role, with the server still enforcing it.
